issues.title: Tailwind classes in incorrect order
issues.description: Tailwind utility classes must follow standard ordering: layout, positioning, sizing, spacing (margin before padding), typography, visual effects. The classes have padding (pr-2) before margin (mt-[-16px]), which violates this convention.
issues.rule_name: Tailwind CSS Classes Must Follow Standard Ordering

issues.title: Missing optional chaining causes runtime error when openForm is undefined
issues.description: The code accesses `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without optional chaining, but openForm can be undefined when rendering certain forms (like the main comment form). The original code correctly used `openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet` with optional chaining. This will cause a "Cannot read property 'in_reply_to_snippet' of undefined" runtime error when the FormWrapper is rendered without an openForm prop, crashing the component.

issues.title: Editor editability incorrectly depends on member expertise instead of name
issues.description: The Form component determines whether the editor should be editable by checking `member?.expertise` instead of `memberName` (which is derived from `member?.name`). According to the comment and the original logic, the editor should be disabled only when the member doesn't have a name or when submitting. Expertise is optional metadata, but name is required for posting. This bug prevents users without expertise from typing in the comment editor, even though they have a valid name and should be allowed to comment.

issues.title: Reply threading broken for nested comments due to incorrect in_reply_to_id
issues.description: The submit function uses `parent.id` as `in_reply_to_id` instead of `openForm.in_reply_to_id`. For nested replies (replying to a reply), these values differ: `openForm.in_reply_to_id` points to the specific comment being replied to, while `parent.id` points to the top-level parent comment. Using `parent.id` breaks the reply chain, causing nested replies to be incorrectly threaded to the wrong comment. This destroys the conversation hierarchy and makes it impossible to track which comment a user is actually replying to in multi-level discussions.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #25858 - 🐛 Fixed reply form showing parent comment author's details

structured_output.summary:
The PR removes the `comment?.member` fallbacks that made the reply form header show the parent comment author's name and expertise. The header now uses only the logged-in member's data. The PR also makes three changes beyond that fix. It drops the `comment` prop from `FormWrapper`, which is a clean cleanup. It changes the editor-enable gate from `member.name` to `member.expertise`, which the PR description never mentions. It changes `in_reply_to_id` in the reply submit from `openForm.in_reply_to_id` to `parent.id`, which is wrong for reply-to-reply forms. The `openForm?.` optional chain was also changed to `openForm.`, and `FormWrapper` is still rendered without `openForm` by the main comment form. That causes a crash when the main form opens.

The header fix itself is correct and the new e2e test targets the reported bug directly. However, the unrelated-looking edits to reply submission and the main form introduce regressions. The main-form crash is severe because it would hit every user who clicks into the top-level comment box.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Blocking: `FormWrapper` dereferences `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without a null check, but `main-form.tsx` renders it with no `openForm`. Focusing the top-level comment box (`isOpen` becomes true) will throw a TypeError. Also blocking: `in_reply_to_id` now uses `parent.id`, but for reply-to-reply forms `parent` is the top-level comment, so replies are posted to the wrong target. The editability gate change needs the author to confirm the intent.

architecture.overview:
Comments-UI renders each comment through `CommentComponent` → `PublishedComment`, which owns the open reply form state (`openCommentForms` in app-context). When a reply form is open, `ReplyFormBox` renders `ReplyForm` (reply-form.tsx) with the `openForm` record and the `parent` comment. `ReplyForm` wraps its `Form` in `FormWrapper`, which is shared with `MainForm`. `FormWrapper` renders the avatar and `FormHeader` from the logged-in member in `useAppContext`. Before this PR, the header fell back to `comment.member` (the comment being replied to) when the current member had no name or expertise, which is the bug.

The PR changes three layers. `FormWrapper` now reads only `member.name` and `member.expertise` and no longer accepts a `comment` prop. `Form` now enables the editor only when `member.expertise` is set. `ReplyForm` now submits `in_reply_to_id: parent.id`, not `openForm.in_reply_to_id`. Reply-to-reply forms are rendered inside the top-level comment, so `parent` and `openForm.in_reply_to_id` differ in that case, and this is where the regression sits.
steps: Entry point: `CommentComponent` / `PublishedComment` in comment.tsx find the open `reply` form from `openCommentForms` and render `ReplyFormBox` for top-level comments. Replies to replies are rendered by the top-level comment with `parent` set to the top-level comment and `openForm.in_reply_to_id` set to the reply being replied to.
`ReplyForm` (reply-form.tsx) builds the submit payload. The PR changes `in_reply_to_id` from `openForm.in_reply_to_id` to `parent.id`, so the reply-to-reply target is lost.

`FormWrapper` (form.tsx) computes the header from `member` only. The PR removes the `comment?.member` fallback and the `comment` prop, which is correct for the header bug. It also changes `openForm?.` to `openForm.`, which breaks `MainForm`.
`Form` (form.tsx) toggles `editor.setEditable` on `member.expertise` instead of `member.name`. This changes which users can type into the reply editor and is not explained in the PR.
`MainForm` (main-form.tsx) renders `FormWrapper` without `openForm`. Its `isOpen` becomes true on editor focus, which now reaches the unguarded `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` access.
Tests: two new e2e cases in actions.test.ts cover the name and expertise header fallbacks. Neither covers reply-to-reply submission nor the main form.

findings.title: Main comment form crashes when opened (openForm undefined)
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx`, `FormWrapper` (around line 313) reads `openForm.in_reply_to_snippet` without a null check. `MainForm` in `main-form.tsx` renders `FormWrapper` without an `openForm` prop, so focusing the main comment box throws a TypeError. Restore the optional chaining (`openForm?.in_reply_to_snippet`) so that `FormWrapper` works without `openForm`. Do not change the `MainForm` call site.

findings.title: Reply-to-reply submits to the top-level comment
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/reply-form.tsx`, the `submit` callback (around line 30) was changed from `in_reply_to_id: openForm.in_reply_to_id` to `in_reply_to_id: parent.id`. For reply-to-reply forms, `parent` is the top-level comment while `openForm.in_reply_to_id` is the specific reply being answered (see `comment.tsx` `openReplyForm`). Restore `in_reply_to_id: openForm.in_reply_to_id` and put `openForm` back in the `useCallback` dependency list. Keep the rest of the PR (removing the `comment` prop from `FormWrapper`) as is.

findings.title: Editor editability silently changed from name to expertise
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx` around line 264, the `useEffect` in `Form` now calls `editor.setEditable(!!member?.expertise && progress !== 'sending')`, but the comment above it still says the editor is disabled when the member has no name. Confirm the intended gate. If the name gate is what's wanted, restore `!!memberName` and the `[editor, memberName, progress]` deps. If expertise gating is intended, update the comment and the PR description to say so. Also check that the 'Reply form does not inherit expertise' e2e test in `apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts` still exercises the intended path.

findings.title: Name-fallback test can pass without checking anything
findings.body:
The second new test asserts `await expect(memberName).not.toHaveText('Named Author')`. Playwright's negated `toHaveText` passes when the locator matches nothing. With `name: null`, the header may not render a `member-name` element at all, so the assertion can pass even if the bug comes back. Pair it with a positive check that the header is in the expected state (for example, the 'Add your name' prompt), or assert the element is visible first. The test also has no reply-to-reply case, so the `in_reply_to_id` regression above is not covered.

::diff{file="apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts" lines="651-680"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `apps/comments-ui/test/e2e/actions.test.ts`, the test 'Reply form does not inherit name from parent comment author' (around line 651-679) ends with `not.toHaveText('Named Author')` on `member-name`. That assertion passes if the element is missing. Add a positive assertion on the expected header state for a member with no name (inspect `FormHeader` in `apps/comments-ui/src/components/content/forms/form.tsx` for the prompt text or testid), so the test fails if the header shows the parent's name. Optionally add a test that a reply-to-reply submits with the correct `in_reply_to_id`.

findings.title: Removing the parent-author fallback fixes the reported header bug
findings.body: The header identity now comes only from `useAppContext().member`, and the `comment` prop is removed from `FormWrapper`, which only the reply form used. The `comment?.member` fallback was the cause of the parent author's name and expertise showing up in the reply header. The first new e2e test reproduces the reported case: a logged-in member with no expertise sees the 'Add your expertise' placeholder instead of 'Head of Comments'.
